endorsements.quote: Large, multicenter, and multimodal datasets must be created for CI, vestibular, and voice applications, and external validation should be required before clinical use.

Tools should be developed in close partnership with clinicians and embedded natively in electronic health records (EHRs), device consoles, and therapy software, rather than as standalone applications.
Institutions should develop AI-specific consent forms, documentation protocols, and internal review boards for quality and safety, modeled after pharmacy and therapeutics committees.

Education and accountability are also vital, AI competency milestones should be integrated into residency and continuing medical education, and quarterly audits for calibration drift, performance parity, and error tracking are essential for long-term safety and trust.

unlisted_practices: Develop ENT-specific AI reporting standards and performance metrics, such as mapping-session duration, missed lesion rates, and validated improvement in voice handicap, building on TRIPOD-AI and CONSORT-AI.
Develop AI-specific patient consent forms for AI use in otolaryngology.
Integrate AI competency milestones into residency and continuing medical education.
Use explainable, auditable, and clinician-supervised AI in ENT.

screen.reason: This is a clinical commentary discussing barriers to real-world AI adoption in otolaryngology and proposing a roadmap for validation, reporting standards, and collaborative governance.
